text.p: - Slovenia's industrial output rose five percent in September compared to the same month in 1995.
- German Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel starts a one-day visit to Slovenia where he will meet the country's president, prime minister and foreign minister.
- An international conference on early discovery of cancer started on Monday at Ljubljana's Medical Faculty.
- Prime Minister Janez Drnovsek visited coal mine Zagorje on Monday to hold talks with miners. The coal mine is expected to be closed down by 2004 and will cost ten billion tolars ($72.5 million).
- The national radio and television station will choose a new general manager on Wednesday from six candidates.
- A French group of experts visited Slovenia on Monday to present French methods of communal administration.
